These notes cover the methods the [proposal](../phd/index.qmd) relies on: the market indicators that form
the evidence, the models that turn it into probability forecasts, and the methods used to judge them. Each
is written from the standpoint of a hypothetical US equities study, with the equation, what it is used for,
and how it would be implemented.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**This is a starting point, not a fixed list.** Methods may be added, replaced or dropped as the research
develops and as the pilot study and supervisory discussion shape the final design.
:::

| Area | Method | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence | [Market indicators](market-indicators/index.qmd): returns, moving-average distance, RSI, realised volatility, volume change, VIX and the variance risk premium | The inputs every model and LLM reads (01, 03) |
| Models | [Regularised logistic regression](logistic-regression/index.qmd) | Interpretable baseline probability forecast (02) |
| | Gradient-boosted trees | Nonlinear benchmark forecast (02) |
| | Long short-term memory network (LSTM) | Compact deep-learning forecast from sequences (02) |
| | Hidden Markov model | Optional regime probabilities (02, 08) |
| | Fixed and adaptive ensembles | The numerical benchmark LLM decisions must beat (02, 10) |
| Evaluation | Brier score and calibration | The primary measure of probability forecasts (10) |
| | Diebold–Mariano test | Whether one forecast is significantly better than another (10) |
| | Walk-forward testing with purging | Testing only on unseen data, without leakage (10) |
| | Sharpe ratio, drawdown and trading costs | The economic result, net of costs (06, 10) |

: Numbers in the last column refer to components of the [system architecture](../phd/architecture.html). Notes for the remaining methods are being added. {.striped}

Each model and evaluation note answers the same questions: what problem it solves, what it assumes, what
data it needs, how it learns, its strengths and weaknesses, how it applies to markets, what the Python
code looks like, and how its outputs are explained.
